text:
alex: Hey team — getting repeated 401 invalid_api_key from hosted API after a key rotation. Calls work in Postman but not from our node server.
jamie: Can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces?
alex: sure, this is what our server ends up sending (weirdly it's using an internal header helper):
```bash
curl -s -i -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Api-Key: sk_live_XXXX..." \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-1","input":"hello"}'
```
alex: Response: HTTP/2 401
{
  "error": {"type": "invalid_api_key", "message": "invalid api key"}
}
jamie: Ah — hosted/managed endpoints expect the Authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. `X-Api-Key` is only accepted by our legacy dedicated/private gateway and is rejected at the hosted edge.
alex: huh — thought both worked. Where's that documented?
jamie: We have a note in API docs under "Authentication" but easy to miss. Quick repro: swap header to `-H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX..."` and retry. Also confirm there are no leading/trailing whitespace or invisible chars.
alex: trying now…
[~30s]
alex: switched to Authorization header and it succeeds, 200. thanks! :tada:
alex: seems our internal http client library maps an env var called `X_API_KEY` into an `X-Api-Key` header by default. I missed that after rotation.
jamie: Good catch. Two suggested follow-ups: 1) rotate the key again if it was accidentally logged in any places that read the env var, 2) update the client mapping to produce `Authorization: Bearer` instead.
erin: Also checking logs on our side — I can see the rejected requests at the edge for your org id 9876, showing header mismatch. No further action needed from infra.
adele: I can add a short note to the quickstart to highlight the header mismatch for hosted vs dedicated (submit PR).
alex: appreciate it. Closing once I verify no other services are still using `X-Api-Key`.
jamie: If anything still fails, drop a curl + raw request capture and we can escalate. :thumbsup:
